QF.id: VIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_117

question.text: A trader is rolling over a short Nifty futures position from the January contract to the February contract. The trader originally shorted January futures at 24,800, buys January back to close it at 24,850, and then sells the February futures at 25,000. What is the trader's loss on closing the January short (per unit)?

answer.text: Rs. 50 per unit loss (24,850 - 24,800), being the buy-back price minus the original short sale price
Rs. 200 per unit (difference between January entry and February entry)
Zero, because the trader maintains the same direction (short) across months

explanation.text: The Logic: The NISM Series VIII workbook (p.33 defines rolling a position over to another futures contract; p.39 defines closing a short by buying back; p.58 supports short-position P&L arithmetic) computes the P&L on a short close as buy-back price minus original short sale price. Here: 24,850 - 24,800 = Rs. 50 per unit loss on the January leg. The February short at 25,000 is a brand new position whose P&L will be determined later by its own settlement/exit price. The Trap: Rs. 200 wrongly subtracts the January entry from the February entry - that is the inter-month spread, not a P&L on closing January. "Zero" ignores that closing the January contract is a separate transaction with its own P&L. Rs. 150 compares the January buy-back price to the February sale price, which is meaningless as a P&L. The audit flagged the original because it asked for "roll-over cost", a term the workbook pages checked do not define, and the stem could also be read as asking for the inter-month spread. Note: The original asked for "roll-over cost", which was ambiguous because the cited NISM Series VIII pages (33, 39, 58) define rolling and short-close P&L but do not define a formula for roll-over cost. The stem has been rewritten to ask specifically for the loss on closing the January short, which the workbook directly supports, making the Rs. 50 per unit figure uniquely correct.
